candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite quantities so their fractional parts are compatible for subtraction by recognizing or creating a common denominator, including rewriting a whole number with a zero fractional part when needed.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A-S01, B-S01, and C-S01 all describe preparing fractions for subtraction through common denominators/equivalent fractions; all also include rewriting whole numbers with 0/n when that serves denominator alignment.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert a mixed number with an improper fractional part into an equivalent standard mixed number before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts identify normalization of improper mixed-number forms as a distinct preprocessing skill. A-S02 and B-S02 are slightly broader because they also mention rewriting whole numbers into mixed-number structure, but that overlap is handled by the alignment skill in C01/C03; the shared core concept across all three is normalization of improper mixed numbers.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into a subtraction-ready whole-and-fraction structure, such as expressing a whole number as a whole plus a zero fraction or decomposing a mixed number into parts.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Only B-S02 explicitly includes a broader restructuring skill beyond normalization, namely rewriting whole numbers as whole + 0/fraction and decomposing mixed numbers into parts as a standalone concept. In A and C, those actions are absorbed into other skills rather than separated.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Carry out the subtraction once forms are compatible, including subtracting numerators of like-denominator fractions and subtracting whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A-S03, B-S03, and C-S03 all represent the main subtraction operation after any needed rewriting or denominator alignment. C-S03 is slightly broader in allowing combination of parts when no borrowing is involved, but the central concept is the same.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units to continue subtraction when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract directly.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: C-S04 isolates borrowing/regrouping, while A-S04 and B-S04 combine borrowing with simplification. The shared concept present in all three is regrouping across whole and fractional parts during subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the subtraction result to lowest terms or an integer form and present the final combined answer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A-S04 and B-S04 explicitly include reducing fractions, simplifying zero fractions, and expressing the final answer as part of the same skill. C does not separate simplification into its own skill and instead limits S04 to borrowing and S03 to subtraction/combining without borrowing.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks share strong agreement on four core concepts: aligning fractional forms, normalizing improper mixed numbers, subtracting aligned parts, and borrowing/regrouping. The main differences are in granularity: Expert C separates borrowing from simplification, while Experts A and B combine them; Expert B also uses a broader rewrite skill that includes both normalization and expressing whole numbers with zero fractional parts. All skill IDs were mapped exactly once, with one-to-many alignment used where A/B bundled concepts that C split apart.
